explain: After a help verb like kan, the next verb is in the infinitive: kan prata.
With no help verb, the verb is in the present tense with -r: hon pratar.
After the help verb vill, use the infinitive: vill dricka.

hint: He drinks tea in the morning.
explain: With no help verb, use the present tense: han dricker.
Bo is a Group III verb: it just adds -r, so jag bor.

prompt: De ska ___ till Stockholm i maj.
hint: They’re going to travel to Stockholm in May.
explain: After the help verb ska, use the infinitive: ska resa.

hint: I usually cook in the evening.
explain: Brukar is a help verb, so the next verb is in the infinitive: brukar laga.
After the help verb måste, use the infinitive: måste jobba.
Stänga is a Group II verb, so the command form drops the -a: Stäng!
Lyssna is a Group I verb, so the command form is the same as the infinitive: Lyssna!
Skriva is a Group IV verb, so the command form drops the -a: Skriv!

hint: You don’t need to book a table at McDonald’s.
explain: “Don’t need to” is behöver inte; Swedish doesn’t use måste inte, and får inte means “not allowed”.

prompt: Vi ___ ta med mat, det finns lunch.
hint: We don’t need to bring food; there is lunch.
explain: Something that isn’t necessary takes behöver inte, never måste inte.

hint: You’re not allowed to smoke here.
explain: Får inte means “not allowed, must not”.
Får means “may, be allowed to”, so Får jag …? asks for permission.
Borde means “ought to, should”.
Brukar means “usually”: jag brukar cykla = I usually cycle.

hint: She wants to become a doctor.
explain: Vill means “want to”.

prompt: Jag är sjuk, jag ___ stanna hemma.
hint: I’m ill, I have to stay at home.
explain: Måste means “must, have to”.
Kunde is the past form of kan: couldn’t = kunde inte.

hint: The children didn’t want to sleep.
explain: Ville is the past form of vill: didn’t want to = ville inte.

prompt: Jag ___ vilja ha en kopp kaffe.
hint: I would like a cup of coffee.
explain: Skulle vilja is the polite way to say “would like”.

hint: She reads a book every week.
ask: Write the verb in the present tense.
explain: Läsa is a Group II verb: the -a becomes -er, so hon läser.

ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After the help verb kan, the verb stays in the infinitive: kan du köra.

ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After the help verb måste, use the infinitive: måste gå.

prompt: Vi ska ___ ett mejl till läraren. (skriva)
hint: We are going to write an email to the teacher.
ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After the help verb ska, use the infinitive: ska skriva.

ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After the help verb vill, use the infinitive: vill dricka.

hint: The children usually sleep late on Saturdays.
ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After the help verb brukar, use the infinitive: brukar sova.

ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After borde, use the infinitive: borde börja.
